test_title: PYST 57: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the nature of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Both the Centre and the States can legislate

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both the Centre and the States can legislate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution contains subjects on which both the Centre and the States can legislate.
 
• It is one of the three lists mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, alongside the Union List and State List.
 
• Under Article 246, the Concurrent List allows both levels of government to legislate on matters such as education, marriage, adoption, forests, and criminal law.
 
• If there is a conflict between the laws made by the Centre and the States on any subject in the Concurrent List, the law enacted by Parliament prevails, as per Article 254.
 
• The Concurrent List ensures cooperative federalism, allowing shared responsibility between the Union and State governments for certain matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exclusively for States**

 
 
• The subjects under the State List in the Seventh Schedule are exclusively under the legislative jurisdiction of State governments.
 
• Examples include police, public health, agriculture, and local governance.
 
• States have autonomy in these areas, ensuring decentralized decision-making and governance.
 
 
 
• **Exclusively for Union**
 
 
• The Union List consists of subjects exclusively under the legislative jurisdiction of the Central Government.
 
• Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and currency.
 
• This ensures centralized control over matters of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Only during emergencies**
 
 
• During a National Emergency, the legislative powers of the States can be temporarily overridden by the Central Government.
 
• Under Articles 352, 356, and 360, Parliament can legislate on subjects in the State List during emergencies.
 
• Such provisions ensure effective governance during crises but are limited to the emergency period.
